Injuries: Owl Scoop says Sheppard was coming back from a right foot injury and RB Sam Brown missed Monday's practice. UAB's Nov. 12 notes flag none. No American report had been published as of this writing.

UAB needs one more win for bowl eligibility for the first time since 2022. The catch is that the Blazers are 5-0 at home and 0-4 on the road, and Owl Scoop notes they've been outscored 131-60 away from Birmingham. UAB's passing defense leads FBS, allowing 122.6 yards through the air per game. End Marlin Dean has 10.5 sacks and five forced fumbles, which ties for the national lead.

Temple is 2-7 but nobody's quitting. Last week at Navy the Owls trailed 28-0 and tied it at 35 before losing late. JoJo Bermudez set a school record with 159 punt-return yards in that game. K.C. Keeler, the winningest active FBS head coach, opened the door for Ajani Sheppard to return from a foot injury: “He's definitely given us a spark when he's gotten in there.”

Defensive tackle Kevin Hornbeak returns from a two-game suspension. “I think Kevin's a guy that wants to be great,” Keeler said. “He's handled it and he's ready to play on senior day.” UAB kicker Jonah Delange is one field goal from tying the school's single-season mark of 22. Philly gets a road-weary team chasing a bowl and a home team sending off its seniors. Keep an eye on every punt. Bermudez can flip this one by himself.

The published card stays Temple Owls −2.5 and Over 48.5 at the numbers it was written against. My final is Temple Owls 27, UAB Blazers 23. Follow The Money's side and total are both pending.

display.story_text:
Market check, Arkansas State at Coastal Carolina: DraftKings CCU -1.5, total 52.5.

Conway closes the home schedule with a full afternoon. Brooks Stadium hosts Senior Day and Salute to Service, and 23 Chanticleers are expected to be recognized before kickoff, per the school. Then the work starts: Coastal is 3-6 and has to win out to reach six wins and a seventh straight bowl.

The number as of Nov. 14, 2026, 4:18 AM ET: ESPN lists DraftKings at CCU -1.5, total 52.5. The Cover Window's published pick is Coastal Carolina -1.5 and Over 50.5. The side still sits at Coastal -1.5 and the total has risen to 52.5, so the card matches on the side and the published Over is now two points under the current total. The card's projected final is Coastal Carolina Chanticleers 27, Arkansas State Red Wolves 24 (Total 51). That pick was published against the Nov. 9, 2026, 9:18 AM ET line, it has not been changed, and this story issues no new one. Prices move, so check yours before kickoff. Full preview at thecoverwindow.com.

Injuries: we found no posted Sun Belt availability list in our check, and neither team's notes flag a key absence.

Arkansas State coach Butch Jones knows where this gets decided. He told the Arkansas Democrat-Gazette that the biggest thing that sticks out about Coastal is the play up front: “They're all fourth- and fifth-year players.” He was blunt about his own front: “We're undersized up front right now in the defensive front. It is what it is.” Louisiana-Monroe ran for 268 yards on the Red Wolves in last week's 19-17 upset.

Quarterback Trey Owens isn't sulking. “There is no reason for us to waver off of one loss,” he said. Cornerback Noah Flores has his eye on Deuce Bailey, who followed coach Ryan Beard from Missouri State and leads the Sun Belt with 19 touchdown passes. Flores said the front has to “create some pressure so we can get him off balance.”

There's a fun side story. Beard guided Missouri State to its first bowl appearance, then left for Coastal before that game, which Arkansas State won 34-28 in the Xbox Bowl. Collin Klein says Blake Barnett and Dillon Duff are both competing, and both could play at Amon G. Carter Stadium.

The number as of Nov. 14, 2026, 4:18 AM ET: ESPN lists DraftKings at TCU -13.5, total 44.5. The Cover Window's published pick is Kansas State +9.5 and Over 46.5. Full preview at thecoverwindow.com.

Injuries and lineup: the Collegian (Nov. 13) reports the Barnett-Duff quarterback competition is unresolved. We found no Big 12 availability list in our check.

K-State is coming off a 66-28 loss to Oklahoma State that Klein called one of the most frustrating losses of his coaching career. Now he gets a defense he respects. “It's their front seven,” Klein said. “They're extremely disruptive. They can rush the passer. They really get off blocks and destroy blocks in the run game.”

TCU is hurting in its own way. The Frogs led Arizona by eight with under seven minutes left last week, then lost 29-28 after a late score, a recovered pooch kick and a field goal with 38 seconds to go. Jaden Craig accounted for all three touchdowns, tight end Kari Ashley caught a career-high 14 passes, and linebacker Hudson Hooper returned an interception 93 yards for a score.

Both teams are 4-5. K-State has won the last three meetings, but its last trip to Fort Worth in 2022 went sideways when TCU erased a 28-10 deficit to win 38-28. ESPN's data capsule has TCU allowing 15.8 points a game, 12th in FBS, and K-State running for 196.8 a game. The Frogs' fans want a finish that doesn't sting. The Wildcats just want to know who's under center.

Bowers Stadium hosts a first Saturday: Sam Houston's first home game under co-interim head coaches Eric Raisbeck and Freddie Aughtry-Lindsay, who took over Oct. 28. The school notes that the Kats will become one of only a handful of FBS programs since 2013 with three head coaches of record in one season, and per NCAA guidance both interims get credit for the same final four games.

The number as of Nov. 14, 2026, 4:18 AM ET: ESPN lists DraftKings at KENN -7, total 46.5. The Cover Window's published pick is Sam Houston +8.5 and Under 47.5. The market is now Kennesaw State -7 with a total of 46.5, so the Kats get a point and a half less than the card did, and the Under is a point above the current total. The card's projected final is Kennesaw State Owls 27, Sam Houston Bearkats 20 (Total 47). Full preview at thecoverwindow.com.

Injuries: we found no posted Conference USA availability report in our check, and Sam Houston's Nov. 12 notes flag none.

Huntsville has a reason to hope that has nothing to do with the record. Since moving to FBS in 2023, Sam Houston is 7-5 in November and 8-25 from August through October, per the school, and November accounted for every one of the program's wins in 2023 and 2025. The Kats are 1-8 and still looking for their first Conference USA win.

This series has a habit of going late. Sam Houston has won all three meetings, every one by seven points or fewer. There was a fourth-down stop at its own 15 with 1:24 left in the 2017 FCS quarterfinals, then Colby Sessums' 35-yard field goal at the horn in 2023 for the program's first FBS win, then a 23-17 overtime win in 2024. The defense has made the biggest jump in FBS against the throw, from 275.9 passing yards a game allowed last year to 161.4 now.

Kennesaw State comes in fresh off a 42-40 win over Delaware. Rickie Collins has 1,687 passing yards and Boogie Woods III has eight rushing touchdowns. Landyn Locke is 37 yards from moving up to 19th on Sam Houston's career passing list, and eight of his 13 touchdown passes this season have gone for 30 yards or more. Two interim coaches, one home crowd and a November habit: Huntsville gets to find out if that habit is real.

The published card stays Sam Houston Bearkats +8.5 and Under 47.5 at the numbers it was written against. My final is Kennesaw State Owls 27, Sam Houston Bearkats 20. Follow The Money's side and total are both pending.

display.story_text:
Springfield starts Homecoming early. Missouri State's game-day themes call for a parade Saturday morning and the coronation of the Homecoming court at halftime at Plaster Stadium, and the school says this campus tradition dates back to 1921. The Bears have won five straight Homecoming games and are 24-21 on Homecoming in their Division I era.

Newest number: ESPN lists DraftKings at Missouri State -1.5, total 49.5, checked Nov. 14, 2026, 4:15 AM ET. Prices move, so check again before kickoff. That is the market's price, not a Cover Window recommendation.

The Cover Window's published pick, unchanged from our game page: Missouri State Bears −1.5 and Over 49.5. Projected: Missouri State Bears 27, New Mexico State Aggies 23 (Total 50). That card was posted against Missouri State Bears −1.5 and a total of 49.5.

Springfield Daily Citizen columnist Collingwood framed it as the latest episode of “Survivor: Bowl Elimination Series,” and he is not wrong. Both teams are 3-6 and 2-3 in Conference USA. He also notes plenty of New Mexico State students may be thinking about Ski Apache by now. Missouri State is 3-1 at home under first-year coach Casey Woods, then has Jacksonville State and Liberty waiting.

The Bears have names worth the trip. Linebacker Jared Lloyd leads the country at 11.33 tackles a game and already has 102. Receiver Jmariyae Robinson is three yards behind current Bears assistant Jermaine Saffold for second in school history in receiving yards, which should make for an interesting staff meeting if he passes a member of his own coaching staff today. Isaiah Myers is 60 yards from a 1,000-yard season and leads FBS with 14 catches of 30-plus yards.

New Mexico State has its own big-play threat. A.J. Williams III caught eight passes for 150 yards and two touchdowns in the 30-14 loss to Liberty, per ESPN's AP capsule, and Hedden threw for 256 there. Missouri State is coming off a 23-20 loss at FIU in which kicker Yousef Obeid went 4-for-4 on field goals to tie a school record.

Injury check: we found no public injury or availability report for either team as of 4:30 AM ET Saturday, Nov. 14. No player status is assumed.

This is about as close to even as the board gets: the published card was set at Missouri State −1.5 and 49.5, and the newest DraftKings number is the same. The case for the home side is the stuff in this story: a 3-1 home record, a five-game Homecoming run and a defense with the nation's leading tackler. The case against is a road team that just got 150 yards from one receiver.

A king and queen get crowned at halftime. The Bears would like the second half to hand Springfield its sixth straight Homecoming win, and send the Aggies home thinking about ski slopes.

The published card stays Missouri State Bears −1.5 and Over 49.5 at the numbers it was written against. My final is Missouri State Bears 27, New Mexico State Aggies 23. Follow The Money's side and total are both pending.

Newark is trying to fit five parties into one afternoon. Delaware's promotional schedule lists Saturday against FIU as Homecoming, Celebration of Champions, Military Appreciation, MVP day and Faculty and Staff Appreciation, all at Delaware Stadium at 3 p.m. If you know somebody who served, this is a good day to bring them.

Newest number: ESPN lists DraftKings at Delaware -3.5, total 54.5, checked Nov. 14, 2026, 4:15 AM ET. Prices move, so check again before kickoff. That is the market's price, not a Cover Window recommendation.

The Cover Window's published pick, unchanged from our game page: Delaware Blue Hens −5.5 and Under 54.5. Projected: Delaware Blue Hens 28, Florida International Panthers 22 (Total 50). That card was posted against Delaware Blue Hens −5.5 and a total of 54.5.

The guy everybody in Newark is watching is Nick Minicucci. Delaware says his 35 completions at Kennesaw State moved him past Super Bowl MVP Joe Flacco for the most completions in a Delaware career, and his 408 yards made him the first Blue Hen with back-to-back 400-yard games. He also tied Flacco's school record with his 11th career 300-yard game. The Hens lost that one 42-40, so the records came with a sour taste.

FIU coach Willie Simmons is not pretending this is easy. “Nick has thrown for a ton of yards and he’s highly efficient,” he told Caplin News. He also gave the best road-trip speech of the week, telling his players to block out the hotel, the bus and the strange locker room: “The one common denominator is 100 by 53 and a third.” Simmons calls his group a “no-name defense,” and lineman Zaire Flournoy said of Delaware's front: “They bring a lot of stuff.”

FIU arrives fresh off a 23-20 win over Missouri State in which Lyons ran 24 times for 216 yards and two scores, per ESPN's AP capsule. Delaware brings Blake Matthews and his five sacks, part of a defense with 23 sacks on the season. These teams met last year in Miami, and Delaware won 38-16.

Injury check: we found no public injury or availability report for either team as of 4:30 AM ET Saturday, Nov. 14. No player status is assumed.

The published card was set at Delaware −5.5 and 54.5; the newest DraftKings number is two points smaller on the side at the same total. The news that matters for the number is the matchup Simmons described: an FIU team that wants to run it and win time against a quarterback with back-to-back 400-yard games. That tension is why this total is sitting in the mid-50s.

Newark gets champions honored, service members saluted and a quarterback chasing the biggest name in Blue Hens history. FIU's nameless defense would love to leave Delaware with everybody learning its name.

display.story_text:
Athens is sold out, according to Georgia's schedule page, and the place has a memory. AP points out that the last time the Bulldogs were No. 1, Auburn came between the hedges four weeks ago and won 27-24. Georgia answered with 27-8 over Florida and 42-7 at Ole Miss, and now the Dawgs are back on top. Kirby Smart is not impressed with that last part. “The ranking means nothing,” he said.

Newest number: ESPN lists DraftKings at Georgia -16.5, total 47.5, checked Nov. 14, 2026, 4:15 AM ET. Prices move, so check again before kickoff. That is the market's price, not a Cover Window recommendation.

Missouri is coming in hot for a different reason. After a 34-20 loss to Texas with a disputed fumble call in the middle of it, athletic director Laird Veatch asked the SEC for a formal review of the officiating, per AP. Eli Drinkwitz drew a hard line on excuses: “We are not victims, and I refuse to give in to being-a-victim mentality.” He also called Georgia “the benchmark for the league right now.”

The best human story is Ahmad Hardy. The Red & Black recounts that he was shot in the upper leg in May in Laurel, Mississippi, and his return was uncertain. He made his season debut at Arkansas on Oct. 31 to a roar from the Missouri crowd, and AP says he is back in a limited role. Jamal Roberts leads the SEC at 119 rushing yards a game. Georgia safety Khalil Barnes: “We know what he is, and we know everything that he can bring to the table.” Missouri has not beaten Georgia since 2013, The Red & Black notes.

Georgia's Gunner Stockton is back in Heisman conversations after four touchdown passes and a rushing score at Ole Miss; he has 20 touchdowns and four interceptions this year. “Explosive player,” lineman Dontrell Glover said. And with officials scrambling for rides Friday, Smart told Paul Finebaum, “We’re wondering how the officials are going to get to where they got to get to,” per Undrafted. Missouri flew in as scheduled.

Injury check: SEC availability report, latest we verified. Georgia (Wednesday report, AJC, posted Nov. 11): DL Joshua Horton questionable, OLB Amaris Williams out; CB Ellis Robinson not listed. Missouri (Thursday night report, On3 Mizzou Today): RB Malae Fonoti (season-ending ACL), OL Josh Atkins and TE Gavin Hoffman among those out.

The published card was set at Georgia −15.5 and 47.5, with a projected 34-17 score. The newest DraftKings number is a point higher on Georgia with the same total. The question for anybody laying that many points is whether Missouri's two-back run game can keep this short, and Georgia's run defense has allowed 83.8 yards a game per AP, best in the SEC.

Sanford Stadium gets a sellout, a top-ranked home team and a running back who fought his way back from a gunshot wound to play football again. Georgia's job is to prove its coach right about the ranking meaning nothing, by playing like it means everything.

The published card stays Georgia Bulldogs −15.5 and Over 47.5 at the numbers it was written against. My final is Georgia Bulldogs 34, Missouri Tigers 17. Follow The Money's side and total are both pending.

The university's hospitality office listed the Thunder from the Sky organ concert at the Basilica of the Sacred Heart, the band's Friday march from the Main Building to Ricci Fields and a Rare Books exhibit on Irish history at Hesburgh Library. Saturday is football, and the Irish come in after beating top-ranked Miami.

Newest number: ESPN lists DraftKings at Notre Dame -29.5, total 51.5, checked Nov. 14, 2026, 4:15 AM ET. Prices move, so check again before kickoff. That is the market's price, not a Cover Window recommendation.

Marcus Freeman brought a history lesson of his own. AP reports he reminded his team of 1993, when Notre Dame upset No. 1 Florida State and then lost at home the next week to Boston College. Running back Nolan James Jr. sounded like he got the message: “We just have to keep doing our job, keep playing the games, winning the games.” James has scored in every game this season.

Freeman's real worry is Mason McKenzie, who leads ACC quarterbacks with 676 rushing yards. “It all starts with the quarterback,” Freeman said. “He can run it, he can throw it.” Bill O'Brien, whose Eagles are 4-5 and have lost 10 straight to Notre Dame, said, “We feel like we’re close, and close is not good enough.” Boston College leads the ACC with 12 interceptions. display.story_text:
Charlottesville is saying thank you today. Virginia's Heroes Appreciation Game runs through the Seats for Service program: every $25 seat a fan buys becomes a seat Virginia Athletics gives to someone who served or is serving now. Up on Grounds, the Cavalier Daily notes it has been 200 years since Edgar Allan Poe was a student here, and the library has a new exhibit on his time at the University.

Newest number: ESPN lists DraftKings at Virginia -11.5, total 46.5, checked Nov. 14, 2026, 4:15 AM ET. Prices move, so check again before kickoff. That is the market's price, not a Cover Window recommendation.

The Cover Window's published pick, unchanged from our game page: Virginia Cavaliers −12.5 and Over 47.5. Projected: Virginia Cavaliers 31, California Golden Bears 17 (Total 48). That card was posted against Virginia Cavaliers −12.5 and a total of 47.5.

Both teams show up on three-game skids. Virginia is 4-1 at home and has won 10 of its last 12 at Scott Stadium since 2025; Cal has won once on the road this year, 21-18 at Syracuse. In last year's first-ever meeting in Berkeley, Kam Robinson's interception with under a minute left sealed a 31-21 Virginia win.

Tony Elliott's message was blunt. “You can't listen to the outside noise,” he told his players, per TheSabre. “This is a good football team that's coming in here, and they're fighting for their season just like us. So, you better strap up and be ready to play.” Cal coach Tosh Lupoi called Beau Pribula's offense, with the most attempted runs in the ACC, a “super exciting challenge.”

The gossip is coming out of Berkeley, on the record. Cal general manager Ron Rivera said on his KNBR show Nov. 5 that Lupoi “has bumped his head a lot,” adding that some advice had been received well and some had not as reported by The Cavalier Daily. Lupoi has switched play callers and quarterbacks, going from Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele to Jackson Brousseau and back.

Injury check: we found no public injury or availability report for either team as of 4:30 AM ET Saturday, Nov. 14. No player status is assumed.

The published card was set at Virginia −12.5 and 47.5, projected 31-17. The newest DraftKings number is a point smaller on the side and a point lower on the total. Two things to weigh: Virginia's strong home record, and a Cal program whose GM is publicly critiquing its first-year coach the week of a cross-country trip.

Scott Stadium has been a good place for Virginia, and today it fills seats with people who served. The Cavaliers would like the only thing leaving Charlottesville in a slump to be the visiting team's bus.

The published card stays Virginia Cavaliers −12.5 and Over 47.5 at the numbers it was written against. My final is Virginia Cavaliers 31, California Golden Bears 17. Follow The Money's side and total are both pending.

Virginia Cavaliers 31, California Golden Bears 17. Virginia Cavaliers cover the 12.5. Over 47.5.

Bloomington has a Broadway show in town and a bigger one at Memorial Stadium. SIX is playing IU Auditorium this weekend, with Saturday shows at 1 and 8 p.m., and in between Indiana gets USC at 3:30 with Big Ten title game and playoff hopes riding on it, per AP. The Daily Hoosier adds the line every Hoosier fan knows by now: Indiana has never beaten USC.

Newest number: ESPN lists DraftKings at Indiana -9.5, total 50.5, checked Nov. 14, 2026, 4:15 AM ET. Prices move, so check again before kickoff. That is the market's price, not a Cover Window recommendation.

The Cover Window's published pick, unchanged from our game page: Indiana Hoosiers −7.5 and Over 49.5. Projected: Indiana Hoosiers 31, USC Trojans 20 (Total 51). That card was posted against Indiana Hoosiers −7.5 and a total of 49.5.

Lincoln Riley is treating a cold Midwest Saturday like a holiday. The forecast AP cited called for a high of 46 and a low of 25. “This is football weather,” Riley said. “Are you kidding me? This is as good as it gets.” USC got in the air before Friday's ground stop, OutKick reported, as cited by Undrafted.

The question of the week is who plays quarterback for the defending national champions. Josh Hoover hurt his throwing arm against Ohio State, and Grant Wilson rallied Indiana to a 23-16 overtime win over Minnesota. “We’ll see how the week plays out and we’ll see who we trot out there,” Curt Cignetti said. Riley shrugged: “I doubt we’re going to see some radically different offense based on who the quarterback is.” If it comes down to a kick, Paddy McAteer hit a program-record 60-yarder against Minnesota.

Receiver Charlie Becker kept it simple: “We're really focused on USC.” USC corner Chasen Johnson called Becker a “real physical guy” with great speed. Indiana will be without running back Turbo Richard, its leading rusher with 745 yards, plus defensive lineman Kellan Wyatt and starting guard Joe Brunner, ESPN reported; linebacker Rolijah Hardy and cornerback A.J. Harris were questionable.

Injury check: Big Ten availability report as reported by ESPN (posted 8:47 PM ET Nov. 11): Indiana RB Turbo Richard, DL Kellan Wyatt and G Joe Brunner out; LB Rolijah Hardy and CB A.J. Harris questionable; QB Josh Hoover not listed. The Hoosiers had not named a starter as of the latest reports we found. Check the game-day report.

The published card was set at Indiana −7.5 and 49.5, projected 31-20. The newest DraftKings number is two points higher on Indiana and a point higher on the total. That move came during a week when Indiana lost its leading rusher and a starting guard and still would not say who its quarterback is, which is worth keeping in mind.

The curtain goes up on SIX at 8 o'clock, and by then Bloomington will know whether its team finally did something that has never been done. USC came to play in the cold on purpose.

The published card stays Indiana Hoosiers −7.5 and Over 49.5 at the numbers it was written against. My final is Indiana Hoosiers 31, USC Trojans 20. Follow The Money's side and total are both pending.

Indiana Hoosiers 31, USC Trojans 20. Indiana Hoosiers cover the 7.5. Over 49.5.

Harris were questionable.

display.story_text:
Eugene's instructions are on Oregon's game center in capital letters: WEAR GREEN. It is a 12:30 local kickoff at Autzen, which leaves time for the Lane County Farmers Market downtown from 9 to 2. It is also, as Dan Lanning put it, the first time Oregon has hosted Michigan since joining the Big Ten. “This will be a fun prep week for us,” he said.

Newest number: ESPN lists DraftKings at Oregon -10.5, total 38.5, checked Nov. 14, 2026, 4:15 AM ET. Prices move, so check again before kickoff. That is the market's price, not a Cover Window recommendation.

The Cover Window's published pick, unchanged from our game page: Oregon Ducks −10.5 and Over 39.5. Projected: Oregon Ducks 29, Michigan Wolverines 15 (Total 44). That card was posted against Oregon Ducks −10.5 and a total of 39.5.

The coaches supplied the gossip themselves. Kyle Whittingham praised Lanning as a “tireless recruiter” on the team's Inside Michigan Football show, then added: “It doesn't hurt that you have $50-plus million at your disposal to, in essence, outbid everybody.” He called it “a credit,” Yahoo Sports reported. HereLansing reports Lanning answered Wednesday by calling Whittingham a Hall of Fame coach and suggesting Michigan might have more for players if it were not paying so much to coaches.

Under the jabs is a real defense. Michigan's notes say the Wolverines rank fourth nationally in yards allowed, have not allowed more than 14 points in a half and have a season high of 21 allowed. Lanning: “Their defense is probably as good as any defense that we’ve played this season.” The offense is the problem; first-year quarterback Tommy Carr threw two interceptions in a 15-6 loss to Michigan State.

Oregon's offense woke up after Lanning fired coordinator Drew Mehringer and promoted Jay Johnson, beating Northwestern and Ohio State. Dylan Raiola, who took over after Dante Moore was hurt, threw for 257 yards at Ohio State without a turnover. The Ducks lost outside rusher Teitum Tuioti for the year with a knee injury. “You don't just replace a guy like Teitum Tuioti,” Lanning said. The series is tied 3-3.

Injury check: Oregon availability report as reported by Ducks on SI (posted 8:06 PM ET Nov. 12): OLB Teitum Tuioti out for the season, QB Dante Moore out, TE Andrew Olesh doubtful, OLB Nasir Wyatt probable. We did not find a Michigan list beyond reports that Tommy Carr is available. Check the game-day report.

The published card was set at Oregon −10.5 and 39.5, projected 29-15. The newest DraftKings number has the same side and a point lower total. A total under 40 says the market trusts Michigan's defense and doubts its offense; Oregon's last two outputs, 34 and 41, are the counterargument.

Autzen gets a sea of green and a Michigan defense that has made a living holding people to 14 in a half. Oregon's new play caller gets the afternoon to find out how much he likes that ceiling.

The published card stays Oregon Ducks −10.5 and Over 39.5 at the numbers it was written against. My final is Oregon Ducks 29, Michigan Wolverines 15. Follow The Money's side and total are both pending.

Oregon Ducks 29, Michigan Wolverines 15. Oregon Ducks cover the 10.5. Over 39.5.

DeKalb has a full house planned in the band section, at least. The Huskie Marching Band's schedule lists Saturday against Nevada as high school senior night, so a stadium of future college students gets a look at Huskie Stadium. Northern Illinois is 0-9, the only winless team in FBS, per Nevada Sports Net, and the people still coming out deserve a lot of credit.

Newest number: ESPN lists DraftKings at Nevada -5.5, total 47.5, checked Nov. 14, 2026, 4:15 AM ET. Prices move, so check again before kickoff. That is the market's price, not a Cover Window recommendation.

The Cover Window's published pick, unchanged from our game page: Northern Illinois Huskies +7 and Over 46.5. Projected: Nevada Wolf Pack 27, Northern Illinois Huskies 21 (Total 48). That card was posted against Nevada Wolf Pack −7 and a total of 46.5.

Nevada coach Jeff Choate is preparing his team for quiet. “I think it's gonna be a BYOE game, bring your own energy,” he said, noting NIU's last home game drew around 7,000 fans by his read of the game sheet. “This is about us.” He also said his team looked like it was “running in cement” in a 31-3 loss to New Mexico, with an illness going around Reno during a short week.

Nevada is 3-6 and starting what the Nevada Appeal calls a three-game quest. The Pack is minus-14 in turnovers, 138th in FBS per ESPN's AP capsule. NIU has a real weapon in DeAree Rogers, with 70 catches for 719 yards, and Dickens threw for 259 in a 30-19 loss to San Jose State.

Injury check: we found no public availability report for either team as of 4:30 AM ET Saturday, Nov. 14.

The published card was set at Nevada −7 and 46.5, projected 27-21, and backs Northern Illinois plus the points. The newest DraftKings number has come down to Nevada −5.5 with the total a point higher. Nevada's minus-14 turnover margin and its illness-and-travel week are the reasons the home side gets points it might not otherwise deserve.

The Huskies have kept showing up every Saturday without a win to show for it, and the band is bringing high school seniors to see the place. One afternoon of energy from the home side would give everybody in DeKalb a story to take home.

The published card stays Northern Illinois Huskies +7 and Over 46.5 at the numbers it was written against. My final is Nevada Wolf Pack 27, Northern Illinois Huskies 21. Follow The Money's side and total are both pending.

Atlanta gets the rivalry with the best argument in the Sun Belt: which school is the real GSU. The AJC says the winner of what fans call “Modern Day Hate” takes the Commissioner's Cup, becomes bowl eligible and gets bragging rights to either “Southern Not State” or “State Not Southern.” It is the third Georgia Grown Bowl, the 13th meeting overall, and the series is tied 6-6, per Georgia State.

Newest number: ESPN lists DraftKings at Georgia Southern -6, total 56.5, checked Nov. 14, 2026, 4:15 AM ET. Prices move, so check again before kickoff. That is the market's price, not a Cover Window recommendation.

Georgia State is also calling it Red, White & Light It Blue Heroes Day at Center Parc Credit Union Stadium. The Panthers arrive hot after a 39-23 win at App State in which Ayden Pereira threw three touchdowns and McCrary ran for 123, per ESPN's AP capsule. Dell McGee kept his message old school: “The bottom line is you’re not going to win the game if you don’t control the line of scrimmage.”

Georgia Southern brings a 49-13 win over Marshall in which Johnson threw four touchdown passes. Receiver Alex Taylor admitted he has been reading the timeline: “I’ve been seeing our fans and they’ve been saying some things about Georgia State on Twitter, which is always fun to look at.” Clay Helton told WSAV there’s a difference between self-assurance and arrogance, and the Eagles have won the last two Georgia Grown Bowls.

Injury check: we found no public injury or availability report for either team as of 4:30 AM ET Saturday, Nov. 14. McGee mentioned working with “the new quarterback” after an earlier loss; we do not assume who starts.

The published card was set at Georgia Southern −5.5 and 56.5, projected 28-25, and takes Georgia State plus the points and the under. The newest DraftKings number is Georgia Southern −6 with the same total. AP's capsule shows two teams that win the clock, both top 25 in time of possession, and that kind of game tends to keep the scoreboard calm.

Both schools answer to GSU, and only one leaves Atlanta with the trophy, the bowl ticket and the hashtag. Choose your shade of blue and get there early.

The AJC says the winner of what fans call “Modern Day Hate” takes the Commissioner's Cup, becomes bowl eligible and gets bragging rights to either “Southern Not State” or “State Not Southern.” It is the third Georgia Grown Bowl, the 13th meeting overall, and the series is tied 6-6, per Georgia State.

Georgia State is also calling it Red, White & Light It Blue Heroes Day at Center Parc Credit Union Stadium. The Panthers arrive hot after a 39-23 win at App State in which Ayden Pereira threw three touchdowns and McCrary ran for 123, per ESPN's AP capsule. Dell McGee kept his message old school: he said you’re not going to win the game if you don’t control the trenches.

Georgia Southern brings a 49-13 win over Marshall in which Johnson threw four touchdown passes. Receiver Alex Taylor admitted he has been reading the timeline: “I’ve been seeing our fans and they’ve been saying some things about Georgia State on Twitter, which is always fun to look at.” Clay Helton told WSAV, “There’s a difference between confidence and arrogance,” and the Eagles have won the last two Georgia Grown Bowls.

Both schools answer to GSU, and only one leaves Atlanta with the trophy, the bowl ticket and the hashtag. Choose your shade of blue and get there early.

My call: Georgia Southern Eagles 28, Georgia State Panthers 25.

Homecoming in Bowling Green has a travel theme this year, per WKU, and the school is asking everybody to wear red for a 2:30 Central kickoff. The Hilltoppers come home 3-6 after losing a 51-42 shootout at Middle Tennessee, a game they tied at 42 in the final minute before it got away.

Newest number: ESPN lists DraftKings at Jacksonville State -7.5, total 54.5, checked Nov. 14, 2026, 4:15 AM ET. Prices move, so check again before kickoff. That is the market's price, not a Cover Window recommendation.

The Cover Window's published pick, unchanged from our game page: Western Kentucky Hilltoppers +7.5 and Under 53.5. Projected: Jacksonville State Gamecocks 30, Western Kentucky Hilltoppers 23 (Total 53). That card was posted against Jacksonville State Gamecocks −7.5 and a total of 53.5.

Tyson Helton sounded like a coach glad to be back on his own grass. “Excited to get back home,” he said. “Got a lot to still play for. They're a good football team. Should be a very competitive game.” His scouting report on Jacksonville State fit in one sentence: “If you want to go win the game against Jacksonville State, you have to contain their quarterback, and that’s hard to do.”

That quarterback is Creel, who threw for 246 yards and ran for 87 more in a 47-14 win over Sam Houston, per ESPN's AP capsule. Jax State is 7-2, and Liberty's game notes say a Liberty win plus a Jax State win today would set the Conference USA title game. WKU's Jonathan Stafford Jr. has 54 catches. Helton's other point, from the WKU Herald: “The explosive plays. Those can’t happen.”

Injury check: we found no public injury or availability report for either team as of 4:30 AM ET Saturday, Nov. 14. No player status is assumed.

The published card was set at Jacksonville State −7.5 and 53.5, projected 30-23, and takes WKU plus the points and the under. The newest DraftKings number is the same side with a point higher total. Helton named the deciding factor himself: contain Creel and cut out the explosive plays, or the number doesn't matter.

Big Red gets to come home from the world tour with the whole Hill in red. The Hilltoppers can make a 7-2 visitor's title-game math a lot messier, which is a fine Homecoming gift.

The published card stays Western Kentucky Hilltoppers +7.5 and Under 53.5 at the numbers it was written against. My final is Jacksonville State Gamecocks 30, Western Kentucky Hilltoppers 23. Follow The Money's side and total are both pending.

Liberty's game notes spell out the stakes: an 8-1 team that can clinch a spot in the Conference USA championship game for the first time since 2023, start league play 6-0 and win nine straight for the first time since the 13-0 start that season. It would also be the Flames' fourth straight win over Middle Tennessee.

Middle Tennessee is no pushover at 5-4. The published card was set at Liberty −21.5 and 53.5, projected 37-14, laying the points and taking the under. The newest DraftKings number is a half-point smaller on the side with the same total. Liberty's ball-control habit is the reason both parts of that card hang together; Middle Tennessee's 51-point week is the risk.

The coins will be gone before kickoff, and Liberty hopes a title-game ticket is in hand by sundown. Middle Tennessee's offense just hung 51 on a rival and would love to spoil the ceremony.

display.story_text:
San Marcos is calling it Heroes Day and Community Day at UFCU Stadium, per Texas State's promotions schedule, and it is the first time these programs have ever played, GV Wire reports. Fresno State got lucky with the sky: its flight left Fresno at 12:25 p.m. Pacific Friday, about an hour before the FAA grounded planes, but was diverted to San Antonio instead of Austin, and the Bulldogs finished the trip by bus.

Newest number: ESPN lists DraftKings at Texas State -9.5, total 59.5, checked Nov. 14, 2026, 4:15 AM ET. Prices move, so check again before kickoff. That is the market's price, not a Cover Window recommendation.

The Cover Window's published pick, unchanged from our game page: Fresno State Bulldogs +9.5 and Under 60.5. Projected: Texas State Bobcats 31, Fresno State Bulldogs 26 (Total 57). That card was posted against Texas State Bobcats −9.5 and a total of 60.5.

G.J. Kinne laid the compliments on thick. “Super, super well coached team, got a lot of respect for those guys,” he said of Fresno State and coach Matt Entz, whom he knows from their FCS days. “Going to be a big-time challenge.” Entz was more worried about his own offense after a 17-10 loss at Utah State that produced 16 rushing yards: “Effort is not a problem. Starkville has Military Appreciation Day at Davis Wade Stadium, and Mississippi State wants everybody in maroon. The kickoff is new: the SEC moved the game to 3:15 p.m. Central (4:15 PM ET), now on SEC Network, because Auburn could not fly Friday. The Tigers rode a bus about five hours from Columbus, Georgia, to Tupelo and got to the team hotel late Friday night, per Auburn on SI and Auburn Undercover.

Newest number: ESPN lists DraftKings at Auburn -2.5, total 51.5, checked Nov. 14, 2026, 4:15 AM ET. Prices move, so check again before kickoff. That is the market's price, not a Cover Window recommendation.

The Cover Window's published pick, unchanged from our game page: Mississippi State Bulldogs +2.5 and Over 50.5. Projected: Mississippi State Bulldogs 28, Auburn Tigers 24 (Total 52). That card was posted against Auburn Tigers −2.5 and a total of 50.5.

Alex Golesh had worried all week about the original start. “This is as early of a start with a legit travel and a bus ride in the morning,” he said Wednesday, asking for “the right focus, the right detail, the right energy level to go start fast.” He got a bus ride the night before and a later kickoff instead. He also gave Mississippi State's run defense a big compliment: “They've not allowed people to run it and that's literally the entire schedule.”

Auburn is the team that went into Athens four weeks ago and beat No. 1 Georgia 27-24, AP noted this week. Byrum Brown ran for more than 120 yards and threw two touchdowns in last week's 26-23 win over Arkansas. Auburn defensive coordinator DJ Durkin on the State quarterback: “He’s got really incredible arm talent.” A.J. Swann threw two touchdowns in a 25-23 loss to Vanderbilt, both to Sanfrisco Magee, who turned two catches into 95 yards. Anthony Evans III has 711 receiving yards.

Injury check: we did not find an SEC availability report for this game in public sources as of 4:30 AM ET Saturday, Nov. 14. Golesh said Wednesday the Tigers “went full go” in practice. No player status is assumed.

The published card was set at Auburn −2.5 and 50.5, projected Mississippi State 28-24, taking State plus the points and the over. The newest DraftKings number we captured is listed in the market note above. The new information since that card is the bus ride; Golesh's own concern was a slow start, and the kickoff move gives his team more rest than it had planned on.

The Famous Maroon Band and a stadium full of maroon get to see whether a team that spent Friday night on a bus can start fast in the late afternoon. Starkville would like the answer to be no.

The published card stays Mississippi State Bulldogs +2.5 and Over 50.5 at the numbers it was written against. My final is Mississippi State Bulldogs 28, Auburn Tigers 24. Follow The Money's side and total are both pending.

display.story_text:
Orlando is loud this weekend even before the Bounce House starts shaking. Downtown, the Warped Tour has two days of punk rock booked on the grounds around the old Citrus Bowl. Out east, UCF hosts Arizona State for the first time ever, in only the third meeting between the programs, per Sun Devils on SI.

Newest number: ESPN lists DraftKings at UCF -3.5, total 47.5, checked Nov. 14, 2026, 4:15 AM ET. Prices move, so check again before kickoff. That is the market's price, not a Cover Window recommendation.

The Cover Window's published pick, unchanged from our game page: UCF Knights −3 and Over 48.5. Projected: UCF Knights 29, Arizona State Sun Devils 24 (Total 53). That card was posted against UCF Knights −3 and a total of 48.5.

The Sun Devils had a rough Friday. On3 reports they were about to leave Phoenix on an American Airlines charter at 4 p.m. Eastern when the FAA stopped every flight in the country. Kenny Dillingham eventually sent the team home rather than keep waiting at the airport, and ASU planned to fly Saturday morning. Kickoff moved to 5:30 p.m. Eastern and from ESPN2 to ESPNU.

Scott Frost has history with the visitors. “Coach Dillingham, and I've known him for a long time,” Frost said, calling Dillingham's brother-in-law one of his better friends. He likes ASU's young quarterback, Jake Fette, and its run defense, and he named what he thinks decides games like this: “The biggest differentiator to me is quarterback play when you have two really even teams.”

Both teams are 5-4. UCF beat Kansas 33-32 last week as Josh Derry caught eight passes for 143 yards, per ESPN's AP capsule, and Alonza Barnett III threw two touchdowns. ASU won 20-10 over Colorado behind Fette and Reed Harris, who has 907 receiving yards and nine touchdowns. Both teams rank in the top 25 in FBS for fewest penalty yards.

Injury check: we found no public injury or availability report for either team as of 4:30 AM ET Saturday, Nov. 14. No player status is assumed.

The published card was set at UCF −3 and 48.5, projected 29-24, laying the points with the over. The newest DraftKings number is a half-point higher on UCF and a point lower on the total. The new information since that card is the travel: ASU flying across the country on game day. That is context for anybody looking at the number now, not a change to a published card.

The Bounce House gets two extra hours to warm up and a visitor that will have spent its morning on a plane. Frost says the quarterback with the special day wins this one, and Orlando would like it to be the one wearing black and gold.

The published card stays UCF Knights −3 and Over 48.5 at the numbers it was written against. My final is UCF Knights 29, Arizona State Sun Devils 24. Follow The Money's side and total are both pending.

UCF Knights 29, Arizona State Sun Devils 24. UCF Knights cover the 3. Over 48.5.

At a Breslin Center pep talk before Michigan State's basketball game Friday night, he talked about what happens when the Spartans win, not if, Yahoo Sports reported. He has reason to feel good: Michigan State beat Michigan 15-6 last week, snapped a six-game losing run and took back the Paul Bunyan Trophy. At 3-6, the Spartans need to win out to reach six wins.

Washington is 5-4 after a 28-25 loss to Penn State, and Chris Lawson has 727 receiving yards, per ESPN's AP capsule. display.story_text:
Huntington's Saturday starts quietly at 10 a.m., at the Memorial Student Center plaza. It is the 56th anniversary of the 1970 crash of Southern Airways Flight 932, which killed all 75 people aboard on the way home from East Carolina, and the annual Memorial Fountain Ceremony brings the town together before anybody thinks about football. The Herd players will be there before they head to Joan C. Edwards Stadium.

Newest number: ESPN lists DraftKings at App State -1.5, total 54.5, checked Nov. 14, 2026, 4:15 AM ET. Prices move, so check again before kickoff. That is the market's price, not a Cover Window recommendation.

This year's keynote speaker is Jeff Heath, who was a 19-year-old Marshall sophomore in 1970 and lost both of his parents and his godparents in the crash, per MetroNews. Athletic director Gerald Harrison remembered speaking at his first ceremony last year: “I look in these families’ faces, and you see the town coming together. It’s a different feeling.” Marshall will wear replica uniforms of the ones worn at East Carolina on Nov. 14, 1970: green helmet with a white stripe, white jerseys, green numerals.

Tony Gibson put it plainly: “This week, we’re playing for a lot more. It’s the anniversary of losing the 75.” His team ran to Spring Hill Cemetery at the start of fall camp, where six players from that team are buried. There is football on the line, too. Both teams are 5-4 and 2-3 in the Sun Belt, and the winner becomes bowl eligible.

Gibson is still sorting out quarterbacks. “It’s a sad thing that we’re going into game 10 and we’re still evaluating,” he said. Khalil Wilkins, the West Virginia transfer who ran for a 66-yard touchdown at Georgia Southern, may see more snaps: “Every time he’s in the game, he makes plays and makes things happen.” App State, which leads the series 17-11, comes in off a 39-23 home loss to Georgia State.

Injury check: we did not find a public availability report for this game as of 4:45 AM ET Saturday, Nov. 14. No player status is assumed; check the teams' game-day reports. Gibson said Wednesday Marshall is still evaluating at quarterback.

The published card was set at App State −1.5 and 53.5, projected Marshall 27-26, taking the Herd plus the points and the under. The newest DraftKings number we captured has the side unchanged at App State −1.5 and the total up a point to 54.5. With an unsettled Marshall quarterback room, a one-point game on the card and a one-point total move, this is about as close to a coin flip as the slate gets.

Marshall is 5-2 when it has played on the anniversary, per the school. Expect the stadium to be full, the throwbacks to be sharp and the noise to come from a place deeper than a Sun Belt title race.

The published card stays Marshall Thundering Herd +1.5 and Under 53.5 at the numbers it was written against. My final is Marshall Thundering Herd 27, App State Mountaineers 26. Follow The Money's side and total are both pending.

Marshall Thundering Herd 27, App State Mountaineers 26. Marshall Thundering Herd cover the 1.5. Under 53.5.

Kroger Field is sold out and dressed for night work. Kentucky's game with Florida carries Night Ops and Salute to Veterans activities with a stadium Black Out, and UK Athletics is asking fans to wear black. It is the fourth home sellout of the season, and the school is warning that Cooper Drive closes four hours before kickoff, so leave early.

Newest number: ESPN lists DraftKings at Kentucky -3, total 52.5, checked Nov. 14, 2026, 4:15 AM ET. Prices move, so check again before kickoff. That is the market's price, not a Cover Window recommendation.

The Cover Window's published pick, unchanged from our game page: Florida Gators +3 and Over 51.5. Projected: Kentucky Wildcats 28, Florida Gators 27 (Total 55). That card was posted against Kentucky Wildcats −3 and a total of 51.5.

Florida touched down Friday with a quarterback change. “Wheels down in Lexington,” the Gators posted, and Gators senior writer Scott Carter reports Aaron Philo is back as the starter after Tramell Jones Jr. went 10 of 22 with two interceptions in last week's 23-7 loss to Oklahoma. Philo has completed 70.5 percent of his passes this year. Florida started 4-0 and has lost four of five since, and it needs one more win to reach a bowl.

Kentucky has its own bruise to shake off, a 34-6 loss at Tennessee that snapped a six-game winning run, per AP. Kenny Minchey set a school record with 242 passes to start a season with only one interception, Carter notes. The Wildcats are the least-penalized team in the SEC; Florida gives up 71.1 penalty yards a game, last in the league. Kentucky has also won three straight at home in this series.

The Gator to watch is Jadan Baugh, third in the SEC with 836 rushing yards, most of it early. After 600 yards in the first four games, he has run for 13, 59, 91, 38 and 35. “Baugh didn't forget how to run,” Carter writes. Somebody has to make defenses stop crowding the box.

Injury check, SEC availability report Friday night, Nov. 13 (KSR/On3): Florida out: WR Vernell Brown III, S Bryce Thornton, LB Jaden Robinson, CB Dijon Johnson (downgraded Friday); DL DK Kalu upgraded to probable. Kentucky: WR Nic Anderson out. Final update comes before kickoff Saturday.

The published card was set at Kentucky −3 and 51.5, projected Kentucky 28-27, taking Florida plus the points and the over. The newest DraftKings number we captured has Kentucky still −3 with the total up a point to 52.5. The new news since that card is Philo back under center and a Florida secondary missing Thornton and Johnson. Both matter to a total, in different directions.

Black shirts, a sold-out house and a Florida team trying to find the offense it had in September. If Baugh gets loose early, Lexington gets nervous; if he doesn't, the Gators could spend a long night in the dark.

The published card stays Florida Gators +3 and Over 51.5 at the numbers it was written against. My final is Kentucky Wildcats 28, Florida Gators 27. Follow The Money's side and total are both pending.

display.story_text:
Provo rearranged its whole Saturday for one airplane. BYU moved kickoff to 5 p.m. Mountain on FOX after Friday's nationwide ground stop kept Baylor in Waco, and the Cougars shifted women's basketball against New Mexico to 1 p.m. and volleyball against Texas Tech to 2 p.m. to make room. Baylor flies out Saturday morning, per the school and KXXV.

Newest number: ESPN lists DraftKings at BYU -8.5, total 50.5, checked Nov. 14, 2026, 4:15 AM ET. Prices move, so check again before kickoff. That is the market's price, not a Cover Window recommendation.

The Cover Window's published pick, unchanged from our game page: Baylor Bears +7.5 and Under 49.5. Projected: BYU Cougars 27, Baylor Bears 21 (Total 48). That card was posted against BYU Cougars −7.5 and a total of 49.5.

There was not much wiggle room. BYU does not play on Sundays, and ESPN's Pete Thamel reported Friday night that the game was likely to be postponed indefinitely if the Bears could not fly, as tracked by Undrafted. Instead, the Big 12 found a Saturday evening slot, and Provo gets a later start instead of an empty Saturday.

BYU comes home stung. Utah beat the Cougars 28-20 last week, and Bear Bachmeier threw four interceptions in the loss, per AP. He still leads the team in rushing, and Legend Glasker had seven catches for 118 yards. Baylor is 6-3 after a 42-31 win over Iowa State in which D.J. Lagway threw two touchdowns and ran for 119 yards. Gavin Freeman has 69 catches.

The Cougars' defense allows 19.8 points a game, 31st in the country, and Baylor's allows 17, 18th. Two good defenses, one tired traveling party.

Injury check: we did not find a public availability report for this game as of 4:45 AM ET Saturday, Nov. 14. No player status is assumed; check the teams' game-day reports.

The published card was set at BYU −7.5 and 49.5, projected 27-21, taking Baylor plus the points and the under. The newest DraftKings number we captured is BYU −8.5 with the total at 50.5, a point toward the Cougars on both. The fresh news is Baylor's same-day flight. The card was made without it and stays as published.

BYU gets a chance to wash the Utah game out of its mouth in front of its own people. Baylor gets the chance to prove a same-day flight is nothing a 6-3 team cannot handle. Somebody is going to be right by about 8:30 Mountain.

The published card stays Baylor Bears +7.5 and Under 49.5 at the numbers it was written against. My final is BYU Cougars 27, Baylor Bears 21. Follow The Money's side and total are both pending.

Kenan Stadium gets Homecoming and its Military Appreciation Game on the same night, per UNC Athletics, and the Tar Heels can make it a celebration with one more win. The Daily Tar Heel points out what that would mean: bowl eligibility, a full turnaround from 4-8 a year ago.

Newest number: ESPN lists DraftKings at Louisville -3.5, total 57.5, checked Nov. 14, 2026, 4:15 AM ET. Prices move, so check again before kickoff. That is the market's price, not a Cover Window recommendation.

The last time Louisville came to Chapel Hill was 2017, and folks here remember it. Lamar Jackson piled up 525 yards in a 47-35 Louisville win, per the Daily Tar Heel. Louisville leads the all-time series 5-3, Card Chronicle notes. It is also UNC's third straight night game at home after five straight noon starts, according to Keeping It Heel.

Bill Belichick was impressed by what is coming: “Getting in on Louisville here, these guys are a really good team. They’re on a good run here. So a lot of good players; they’re pretty tough offensively.” He has reason. The Cardinals score 40.8 points a game, sixth in the country, per AP, and quarterback Lincoln Kienholz has 2,276 passing yards and 11 rushing touchdowns.

Billy Edwards Jr. is coming off his two best games as a Tar Heel, with four touchdown passes against Miami and a 76 percent day at UConn, per Card Chronicle. His tight end, Jelani Thurman, just matched Mike Chatham's 1979 mark of eight touchdowns in a season, per the Daily Tar Heel. “It’s an out-execution kind of game now,” Edwards said. “That’s what it will come down to at the end of the day.”

display.story_text:
The Commander-in-Chief's Trophy is back at the Air Force Academy, and this is the first home game since the Falcons won it 24-21 at Army, their first CIC title since 2022. The Academy's event page says Falcon Alley opens three hours before the 5 p.m. Mountain kickoff, the team arrives to the Drum and Bugle Corps, and the Wings of Blue parachute team drops in about 20 minutes before kickoff.

Newest number: ESPN lists DraftKings at Air Force -13.5, total 48.5, checked Nov. 14, 2026, 4:15 AM ET. Prices move, so check again before kickoff. That is the market's price, not a Cover Window recommendation.

The Cover Window's published pick, unchanged from our game page: San José State Spartans +11.5 and Over 47.5. Projected: Air Force Falcons 29, San José State Spartans 19 (Total 48). That card was posted against Air Force Falcons −11.5 and a total of 47.5.

The visiting coach has seen the Falcons' offense more than most people alive. San José State's Ken Niumatalolo spent years at Navy, and The Gazette notes his two games against Air Force with the Spartans ended in a 1-1 split, 33-33 combined, with the Falcons held about 40 rushing yards under their usual pace. “Coach Ken knows how to play against us,” center Rudy Varela said. “I’m really excited to play against these guys.”

Defensive end Jaylin Reese is worried about the trophy hangover, not the trophy. “We kind of already made the mistake on defense,” he said, pointing to a slip at NIU after a good game against Navy. “Winning’s a lot more fun than losing, so we’re trying to keep that up.” The Spartans throw for 228.2 yards a game, a long way from Army's 80.8.

San José State had its own Friday problem. Gophers Nation listed the Spartans among the teams still grounded Friday afternoon; no kickoff change has been announced.

Injury check: we did not find a public availability report for this game as of 4:45 AM ET Saturday, Nov. 14. No player status is assumed; check the teams' game-day reports.

The published card was set at Air Force −11.5 and 47.5, projected 29-19, taking San José State plus the points and the over. The newest DraftKings number we captured is Air Force −13.5 with the total up a point to 48.5. The side has moved two points toward the Falcons, which gives a plus-the-points card more cushion at the current price. The card itself stays as published at 11.5.

A parachute team, a trophy on display and a coach on the other sideline who has spent a career figuring out this offense. Air Force wants to show the Army win was a beginning, not a peak.

The published card stays San José State Spartans +11.5 and Over 47.5 at the numbers it was written against. My final is Air Force Falcons 29, San José State Spartans 19. Follow The Money's side and total are both pending.

Mobile hosts the Battle for the Belt tonight at Hancock Whitney Stadium, AL.com reports, and both sides walk in with the same 4-5 record and the same 2-3 Sun Belt mark. Neither team can afford a loss with a bowl trip on the line.

Newest number: ESPN lists DraftKings at South Alabama -3, total 55.5, checked Nov. 14, 2026, 4:15 AM ET. Prices move, so check again before kickoff. That is the market's price, not a Cover Window recommendation.

The Cover Window's published pick, unchanged from our game page: South Alabama Jaguars −2.5 and Over 55.5. Projected: South Alabama Jaguars 30, Troy Trojans 27 (Total 57). That card was posted against South Alabama Jaguars −2.5 and a total of 55.5.

Troy coach Parker sounded like a man tired of watching tape. After a 41-17 loss to Louisiana Tech, he said: “All hands on deck to figure out what we will do for us to play better offensive football. We have to play better on offense and I think those that love us, and those that are mad at me right now, go look at the tape.” The Troy Messenger reports Goose Crowder is listed as the starting quarterback.

Parker also wants steadiness more than a big week of practice. “I am more concerned about us playing more consistent football on game day,” he said. Two weeks ago his team upset James Madison, then came last Saturday's dud. That is the roller coaster the Messenger describes.

South Alabama runs for 207.1 yards a game, 18th in the country, and comes in off a 28-26 loss to Louisiana in which Bishop Davenport ran for two touchdowns, per AP.

Tulsa's Homecoming got pushed into the evening, and H.A. Chapman Stadium gets a doubleheader out of it. The American Conference men's soccer championship goes at 3 p.m. Central, then football at 6:15 p.m. Central, per News On 6. Tickets already bought for either event stay good.

Newest number: ESPN lists DraftKings at Tulsa -6.5, total 73.5, checked Nov. 14, 2026, 4:15 AM ET. Prices move, so check again before kickoff. That is the market's price, not a Cover Window recommendation.

FAU had a Friday nobody should repeat. WPBF reports the Owls switched to a different charter because of a mechanical problem, then sat in buses on the tarmac at Fort Lauderdale for about an hour before going back to campus in Boca Raton. Athletic director Josh McCowan said, “Our team will fly to Tulsa tomorrow morning for a game that will now be played tomorrow at (6:15 p.m. CT) on ESPN+.”

The Owls bring a serious offense with them. Caden Veltkamp has 27 touchdown passes and five interceptions, and Easton Messer has 976 receiving yards and 12 scores, per AP. FAU scored 60 on UTSA last time out. Tulsa scored 60 on Tulane, with Baylor Hayes throwing four touchdowns and Oran Singleton catching 13 passes for 177 yards and three scores.

Tulsa is fourth in the country at plus-12 in turnovers. FAU leads the series 4-1 coming into the sixth meeting, per Tulsa Athletics.

display.story_text:
Tiger Stadium closes its home schedule with a big one. LSU says this is the first meeting in Tiger Stadium between LSU and Texas since 1953, on Senior Night, with LED bracelets for the crowd and Bert Jones, the Tigers' first All-American quarterback, getting his jersey retired at halftime. LSU lists kickoff at 6:45 p.m. Central on ABC.

Newest number: ESPN lists DraftKings at LSU -4.5, total 46.5, checked Nov. 14, 2026, 4:15 AM ET. Prices move, so check again before kickoff. That is the market's price, not a Cover Window recommendation.

The Tigers walk down Victory Hill at 4:46 p.m. Central, by LSU's own timeline, and the Golden Band from Tigerland follows a few minutes later. Texas almost missed the parade. The Longhorns took off from Austin just after 10 p.m. Central Friday and were expected in Baton Rouge before midnight, according to Horns247 reports cited by Burnt Orange Nation and tracked by Undrafted.

Arch Manning grew up in New Orleans and went to big LSU home games as a kid, AP notes. Now he gets a Saturday night in Death Valley against a defense that has 36 sacks, third in the country, led by Princewill Umanmielen with 8.5. Texas has given up 27. Steve Sarkisian called LSU “arguably the most talented team” Texas will face: “It’s hard to see how they lost three games.”

Lane Kiffin has heard the noise after a 31-13 home loss to Alabama. “The basketball hoop’s stupid, and they shouldn’t have a little kid on the smoke machine,” he said, summing up the critics. “I just know all that’s what comes when you lose. When you win, it’s all different.” He also said this: “The games that we’ve needed to finish we’ve gone 0-for-3.” Kiffin and Sarkisian are old friends from USC and Alabama, and Sarkisian recalled Pete Carroll's lesson that “there’s nothing more gratifying than beating your friends.”

Injury check, SEC availability report Friday, Nov. 13 (Inside Texas/On3): Texas out: LT Trevor Goosby, RB Hollywood Smothers, TE Nick Townsend, DE Richard Wesley; DT Hero Kanu probable; OL Cole Hutson questionable. WR Cam Coleman and DE Colin Simmons were not on the report all week. LSU: LB Whit Weeks questionable, OT Weston Davis probable, four players out.

The published card was set at LSU −3.5 and 45.5, projected LSU 25-24, taking Texas plus the points and the over. The newest DraftKings number we captured is LSU −4.5 with the total at 46.5, a point toward LSU on the side and a point up on the total. The new information since that card is Texas' late Friday flight and Simmons off the report. The card stays as published.

A jersey goes up in the rafters, a Louisiana kid comes home in the other team's colors and two old friends try to beat each other. Death Valley at night does not need more than that.

The published card stays Texas Longhorns +3.5 and Over 45.5 at the numbers it was written against. My final is LSU Tigers 25, Texas Longhorns 24. Follow The Money's side and total are both pending.

LSU Tigers 25, Texas Longhorns 24. Texas Longhorns cover the 3.5. Over 45.5.

display.story_text:
Getting to Blacksburg is part of the test. The Stanford Daily says the Cardinal's last long road trip of the year turned into a two-plane, two-hotel trip, because there is no major airport anywhere near the place. Hokies coach James Franklin has been talking about that lack of a nearby airport, too.

Newest number: ESPN lists DraftKings at Virginia Tech -15.5, total 57.5, checked Nov. 14, 2026, 4:15 AM ET. Prices move, so check again before kickoff. That is the market's price, not a Cover Window recommendation.

The Cover Window's published pick, unchanged from our game page: Virginia Tech Hokies −15.5 and Under 59.5. Projected: Virginia Tech Hokies 37, Stanford Cardinal 20 (Total 57). That card was posted against Virginia Tech Hokies −15.5 and a total of 59.5.

Waiting at Lane Stadium is a theme night for Ag Day and Veterans Day, per Virginia Tech on SI, in a mountain town of about 45,000 that empties into the stadium. Stanford offensive coordinator Terry Heffernan, who spent three years at Virginia, told the Daily the whole town shows up and the place rocks.

Stanford is 4-5 and needs two of its last three to reach a bowl. Senior receiver Caden High called the locker room “very optimistic and confident.” Virginia Tech is 6-3 but coming off a 51-28 loss to SMU that was close until SMU scored 21 straight points to start the second half, per the Daily.

Ethan Grunkemeyer has thrown for 2,431 yards and 18 touchdowns with three interceptions, and Jeffrey Overton Jr. has 762 rushing yards, per AP. Heffernan thinks there is room to throw: “SMU was able to find some cracks, and we feel like we’ve got a pretty good game plan for that.”

Injury check: we did not find a public availability report for this game as of 4:45 AM ET Saturday, Nov. 14. No player status is assumed; check the teams' game-day reports.

The newest DraftKings number we captured has the side unchanged at Virginia Tech −15.5 and the total down two points to 57.5. The total has moved toward the card's under. The card stays as published.

Two flights, two hotels and one loud stadium at the end of the road. Stanford says it has a plan for the cracks; Blacksburg intends to fill them with noise.

The published card stays Virginia Tech Hokies −15.5 and Under 59.5 at the numbers it was written against. My final is Virginia Tech Hokies 37, Stanford Cardinal 20. Follow The Money's side and total are both pending.

Shane Beamer said Thursday, “He has worked really, really hard to get himself back to where he feels, and we feel, good about him being out there on Saturday night. He’s gotten better each day in practice.”

Offensive coordinator Kendal Briles, who used to run Arkansas' offense, gave the Hogs' best defender a compliment: “We know where 97’s lined up. I can tell you that.” That is Quincy Rhodes, and Auburn sacked K.J. Jackson six times last week. The Post and Courier wants the Gamecocks to rely on the run to spare Sellers; Arkansas allows 156.3 rushing yards a game, per AP.

The Gamecocks' defense has something to fix, too. The Post and Courier notes South Carolina somehow ran three straight plays with 10 men on the field during A&M's last drive.

The last time UTEP hosted Wyoming, it was Nov. 25, 1995. The Miners say tonight's 34th meeting is Senior Night at the Sun Bowl, 8 p.m. Mountain on FS1.

The Cowboys made it, barely. The El Paso Times reported Wyoming's trip was delayed about five hours by the ground stop, and the Cowboys were in the air for El Paso shortly after flights resumed around 7 p.m. Mountain. Kickoff stays put.

Wyoming is 6-3 and just won a 41-35 game over UNLV in which Samuel Harris ran for 128 yards and two touchdowns, per AP. Tyler Hughes leads the team in passing and rushing. UTEP is 1-8 after a 17-14 loss to Hawai'i, and its seniors would love to go out with a win their families will remember.

A rivalry that skipped three decades, Senior Night under the Franklin Mountains and a visitor that landed late. UTEP would like one big night to remember 2026 by.

UTEP allows 34.3 points a game, so Wyoming should get to the mid-20s or better, and the Miners need only their 14.1 a game, plus a little more, to get it over. The posted number dropped from 43.5 to 40.5, and my 45 combined points clear it.

The risk is UTEP's offense. The Miners have scored 14 or fewer in seven of nine games, and the quarterback spot has moved between EJ Colson Jr. and Raymond Moore III. If Wyoming's defense, led by Esaia Bogar and his 5.5 sacks, holds the Miners to single digits, both of my picks are in trouble.

The published card stays UTEP Miners +9.5 and Over 40.5 at the numbers it was written against. My final is Wyoming Cowboys 27, UTEP Miners 18. Follow The Money's side and total are both pending.

A team that practiced on a runway against a team still waiting for its big win of the year. Pullman would like that win to come tonight, and the Cougs have a defense in front of them that has not stopped many people.

The published card stays Colorado State Rams +9.5 and Under 67.5 at the numbers it was written against. My final is Washington State Cougars 35, Colorado State Rams 27. Follow The Money's side and total are both pending.

display.story_text:
North Dakota State's traveling party was inside the theater at the USS Arizona Memorial, watching the 23-minute film about the Pearl Harbor attack, when phones lit up with the news that the FAA had stopped every flight in the country. “We’re watching a movie about a World War, and to get out of the theatre and see all the texts was pretty remarkable,” coach Tim Polasek told InForum. “Obviously we’re thankful to be here so we get a chance to play a football game.”

Newest number: ESPN lists DraftKings at North Dakota State -7, total 38.5, checked Nov. 14, 2026, 4:15 AM ET. Prices move, so check again before kickoff. That is the market's price, not a Cover Window recommendation.

The Cover Window's published pick, unchanged from our game page: North Dakota State Bison −6.5 and Over 38.5. Projected: North Dakota State Bison 25, Hawai'i Rainbow Warriors 18 (Total 43). That card was posted against North Dakota State Bison −6.5 and a total of 38.5.

They were lucky to be there at all. InForum says mechanical trouble with the charter pushed the Bison's Thursday 11:30 a.m. departure from Fargo to just before 1 a.m. Friday, and the team landed in Honolulu at 4:45 a.m. local time. Athletic director Matt Larsen: “nothing surprises you with this group of guys and I think they’ve handled it really well.”

Hawai'i calls it Military Night, per its game themes, a fitting one for a Veterans Day weekend and a visitor fresh off a Pearl Harbor visit. It is the first meeting between these programs. The Rainbow Warriors are 3-6 and looking for a third straight win after a 17-14 victory over UTEP in which Micah Alejado threw for 303 yards, per AP.

NDSU's defense allows 11.9 points a game, second in FBS, and its red-zone defense ranks first, per AP. Hawai'i ranks 133rd in red-zone offense. Points will be hard to find at the Ching Complex.

Injury check: we did not find a public availability report for this game as of 4:45 AM ET Saturday, Nov. 14. No player status is assumed; check the teams' game-day reports. Polasek said he would not know until Saturday morning whether the 13-hour delay had any effect on his players.

The newest DraftKings number we captured is North Dakota State −7 with the total unchanged at 38.5. A half-point move onto 7 is worth knowing. The card stays as published at 6.5.

A visitor that saw Pearl Harbor the day before kickoff, Military Night in Manoa and a first-ever meeting at 6 p.m. Hawaii time. College football's last kickoff of the night has more meaning than most.

The published card stays North Dakota State Bison −6.5 and Over 38.5 at the numbers it was written against. My final is North Dakota State Bison 25, Hawai'i Rainbow Warriors 18. Follow The Money's side and total are both pending.

display.story_text:
Ole Miss at Oklahoma lands on American Heritage Saturday in Norman, a 4:15 p.m. ET date at Gaylord Family Oklahoma Memorial Stadium for two SEC teams that both need a November answer. My Ole Miss vs Oklahoma prediction is Ole Miss Rebels 25, Oklahoma Sooners 22, with Ole Miss Rebels −1.5 and Under 49.5.

Langston Fairbanks, the Rebels insider, talks like the visitors already own the loudest voice. "Trinidad Chambliss has 18 touchdowns. We can win in Norman." Savannah Redbird-Lowe, Oklahoma's insider, answers with John Mateer. "15 touchdowns. We just won at Florida. Your number is still a road number."

The market flipped. DraftKings opened Oklahoma −4 with 53.5 on the over/under, and by Monday morning it was Ole Miss −1.5 with 49.5. I will take the visitor at this price. Ole Miss scores 33.8 a game. Oklahoma allows 19.2. That sounds like a problem until you remember Ole Miss just lost 7-42 to Georgia and Oklahoma just won 23-7 at Florida. The open had Oklahoma as a home favorite. The move put Ole Miss in the spot of laying points on the road. I trust the Rebels' offense more than I trust Oklahoma's recent scoring pace of 22.1 points a game.

Chambliss has 2,359 passing yards. Deuce Alexander has 669 receiving yards. Kewan Lacy has five rushing scores. Mateer has 2,042 yards. Isaiah Sategna III has 625 receiving yards. Lloyd Avant has 394 rushing yards. One quarterback just got punched by Georgia. The other just controlled Florida. I still think Chambliss answers first in a one-possession game.

The Under is about Oklahoma's ceiling and Ole Miss's last script. The Georgia game finished at 49 combined points with almost all of them on one side. Oklahoma's Florida win finished at 30. My 47 points sit under 49.5, and the market already cut four points off the open.

The side divides the room. The Formula has Ole Miss Rebels −1.5 and likes Over 49.5 at 26-24. Next Man Up likes Oklahoma Sooners +1.5 and Under 49.5 at 25-23. Letdown Watch likes Ole Miss Rebels −1.5 and Under 49.5 at 26-22. In The Trenches has no side and no over/under call this week. Follow The Money's side and total are both pending.

Letdown Watch: "Next Man Up took the home points after the market flipped." Next Man Up: "Mateer just won in Gainesville. The flip can wait."

American Heritage gets the theme. Ole Miss get a road one-possession win in a total that already came down.

Ole Miss Rebels 25, Oklahoma Sooners 22. Ole Miss Rebels cover the 1.5. Under 49.5.

display.fanatic_story:
Ole Miss Rebels vs Oklahoma Sooners is American Heritage Saturday in Norman, a late-afternoon kickoff at Gaylord Family Oklahoma Memorial Stadium for two SEC teams carrying very different memories from last week. Langston Fairbanks shows up talking about Trinidad Chambliss like the Georgia loss was a closed book. Savannah Redbird-Lowe arrives with John Mateer's Florida tape and a reminder that Norman still expects the home team to finish.

Langston: Chambliss has 18 touchdowns. Alexander can win the route. We did not come to Norman to be quiet.

Savannah: Mateer just won at Florida. Avant runs between the tackles. Your quiet still has to deal with that.

Ole Miss is coming off a 7-42 loss to Georgia that emptied the air out of an otherwise productive offense. Oklahoma is coming off a 23-7 win at Florida that looked like the version of this team the preseason promised. The Rebels still score 33.8 points a game and allow 26.0. The Sooners score 22.1 and allow 19.2. That is a collision between a visitor that can put up points and a home team that has spent November trying to remember how.

Trinidad Chambliss has 2,359 passing yards with 18 touchdowns and nine interceptions. Deuce Alexander has 669 receiving yards. Kewan Lacy has 388 rushing yards and five scores. Blake Purchase has 4.5 sacks. Keaton Thomas has 55 tackles. When Chambliss is clean, Ole Miss looks like the team that hung crooked numbers earlier this fall. When he is not, Georgia tape starts replaying itself.

Oklahoma's answer is Mateer and a defense that just held Florida to seven. Mateer has 2,042 yards with 15 touchdowns. Isaiah Sategna III has 625 receiving yards. Lloyd Avant has 394 rushing yards. Adepoju Adebawore has 4 sacks. Owen Heinecke has 73 tackles. The Sooners do not need a track meet. They need to keep Chambliss uncomfortable and let Mateer win a one-possession game in front of the home crowd.

Savannah: American Heritage is nice. A third-down sack is nicer.

Langston: Themes are nice. Chambliss on schedule is nicer.

Norman will treat the afternoon like a statement chance after Florida. Ole Miss will treat it like a reset after Georgia. One of those moods usually wins in November, and Memorial Stadium will decide which one before the lights take over the evening.

Langston will talk Chambliss. Savannah will talk Mateer. American Heritage will talk about whether the home team finished the job.

American Heritage Saturday is not Military Appreciation — that theme lands next week against Texas A&M — but it still puts Norman in a reflective mood before a game that feels like a measuring stick. Ole Miss wants to prove Georgia was an outlier. Oklahoma wants to prove Florida was a beginning. Those two proofs cannot both be true by the end of the night.

Langston keeps talking about Chambliss. Savannah keeps talking about Mateer. Memorial Stadium will decide which November story gets to keep going.

Norman in mid-November is loud even when the theme is reflective. American Heritage Saturday puts history on the pregame board and then asks two quarterbacks to write a new chapter anyway. Chambliss has the volume numbers. Mateer has the fresher win. Ole Miss has the higher scoring pace. Oklahoma has the home crowd and the harder defense. That is enough material for a one-possession game that will not feel decided until somebody blinks on fourth down.

The Georgia hangover is real. The Florida bounce is real. Memorial Stadium gets to choose which one was louder.

One possession. Two quarterbacks. A Norman evening that will not feel settled early.

Norman never settles down, and the Rebels fly home anyway. My call: Ole Miss Rebels 25, Oklahoma Sooners 22.

Ole Miss at Oklahoma lands on American Heritage Saturday in Norman, a 4:15 p.m. ET date at Gaylord Family Oklahoma Memorial Stadium for two SEC teams that both need a November answer. My Ole Miss vs Oklahoma prediction is Ole Miss Rebels 25, Oklahoma Sooners 22, with Ole Miss Rebels −1.5 and Under 49.5.

Langston Fairbanks, the Rebels insider, talks like the visitors already own the loudest voice. "Trinidad Chambliss has 18 touchdowns. We can win in Norman." Savannah Redbird-Lowe, Oklahoma's insider, answers with John Mateer. "15 touchdowns. We just won at Florida. Your number is still a road number."

The market flipped. DraftKings opened Oklahoma −4 with 53.5 on the over/under, and by Monday morning it was Ole Miss −1.5 with 49.5. I will take the visitor at this price. Ole Miss scores 33.8 a game. Oklahoma allows 19.2. That sounds like a problem until you remember Ole Miss just lost 7-42 to Georgia and Oklahoma just won 23-7 at Florida. The open had Oklahoma as a home favorite. The move put Ole Miss in the spot of laying points on the road. I trust the Rebels' offense more than I trust Oklahoma's recent scoring pace of 22.1 points a game.

Chambliss has 2,359 passing yards. Deuce Alexander has 669 receiving yards. Kewan Lacy has five rushing scores. Mateer has 2,042 yards. Isaiah Sategna III has 625 receiving yards. Lloyd Avant has 394 rushing yards. One quarterback just got punched by Georgia. The other just controlled Florida. I still think Chambliss answers first in a one-possession game.

The Under is about Oklahoma's ceiling and Ole Miss's last script. The Georgia game finished at 49 combined points with almost all of them on one side. Oklahoma's Florida win finished at 30. My 47 points sit under 49.5, and the market already cut four points off the open.

The side divides the room. The Formula has Ole Miss Rebels −1.5 and likes Over 49.5 at 26-24. Next Man Up likes Oklahoma Sooners +1.5 and Under 49.5 at 25-23. Letdown Watch likes Ole Miss Rebels −1.5 and Under 49.5 at 26-22. In The Trenches has no side and no over/under call this week. Follow The Money's side and total are both pending.

Letdown Watch: "Next Man Up took the home points after the market flipped." Next Man Up: "Mateer just won in Gainesville. The flip can wait."

American Heritage gets the theme. Ole Miss get a road one-possession win in a total that already came down.

Ole Miss Rebels 25, Oklahoma Sooners 22. Ole Miss Rebels cover the 1.5. Under 49.5.
